usageNotes: Use this to read the current firewall configuration (enabled state, default policies, logging levels, and protocol-level options such as DHCP, NDP, MAC filtering, and IP filters) for a specific QEMU VM on a remote PVE cluster. The caller must hold the Resource.Audit privilege on the remote/vmid resource. If the VM spans multiple nodes, pass the optional 'node' query parameter to target the correct host; omitting it lets PDM resolve the node automatically.

examples.summary: Read firewall options for VM 101 on remote 'pve-hetzner'

tips: All returned fields are optional — a field absent from the response means the cluster is using the documented default (e.g., macfilter defaults to true, enable defaults to false).
policy_in and policy_out have no documented default; if omitted the effective policy is determined by the cluster-level firewall configuration.
log_level_in and log_level_out default to 'nolog', so firewall hits are silent unless explicitly set to a syslog severity level.
ipfilter=true implicitly creates empty ipfilter-net ipsets per interface, which restrict IPv6 link-local addresses — useful hardening for multi-tenant environments.
This endpoint is read-only; use the corresponding PUT/POST endpoint to change options.
